items.name: Geometry and measurement
items.basis: Live AutoCAD run drew lines, arcs, circles, polylines, rectangles and two boundary hatches through a 90-step CADPlan, then scan_all_entities read back 81 entities (Length/Area taken from COM read-back) with zero-issue geometry validation. The pure-Python topology layer (closed profiles across entities, line-curve intersections, coplanarity, unitless arc angles left unresolved, budget failures fail atomically) has many ordinary/boundary/adversarial regression tests that ran green in CI on the pinned SHA. Strict pass: probes P01/P02 executed the cross-entity topology on real code: a 4-line 10x5 rectangle gives exactly one closed profile of area 50, while an open chain and a 0.001 gap give none. The full suite passed (454). Probe P15, however, shows draw_line reporting 'OK: ... handle: (empty)' when the controller returned {success: false, 'Unable to connect to AutoCAD'}: the tool never checks the controller result. draw_circle raises instead.
items.scope_and_limits: Creation paths are traced unchanged except lint since the live run. Topology tests use real production code over a SQLite fixture, not AutoCAD. No saved/reopened or cross-process independent check of measurements; the committed DWG is not re-read by the repo. Freshly drawn entities are cached in SQLite from input arguments (draw_circle area uses 3.14159) until a rescan. Live AutoCAD artifacts were recorded 2026-08-08..10 (commits bdb6c25/d986289/b02d0fa). Since then creation/annotation/hatch/table/array/delete paths changed only by lint; move/copy/rotate/scale and all LISP-based edits (trim/extend/fillet/break/join/stretch), connection ProgID logic, DXF import and selection changed, so those are not covered by the live artifacts.

deduction.reason: Cap at 2: serious demonstrated false-success. With AutoCAD disconnected, draw_line reports a drawn line (probe P15; drawing_tools.py treats the controller's failure dict as the entity). Topology code passed its executed probes.

items.name: Editing
items.basis: Live flange-coupling demo executed move_entity, array_rectangular, array_polar, delete_entity and edit_table_cell through CADPlans with a 91-entity rescan afterwards. Mocked unit tests now check that a failed move/copy is not reported as success and that edited geometry is marked stale. Strict pass: probe P09 reproduced the trim/extend defect at the wrapper level. With a stub document that executes nothing, trim(['FFFF0']) and extend() return success=true, and trim_entity reports 'OK: trimmed FFFF2'; nothing is read back. Real AutoCAD editing was not executable.
items.scope_and_limits: Array/delete/table paths are traced unchanged; move/copy changed after the live run and are covered only by mocked tests. trim/extend/fillet/break/join/stretch have no output evidence. Source shows trim/extend report success whenever the LISP command returns to idle, without checking that geometry changed (see serious_defects). Live AutoCAD artifacts were recorded 2026-08-08..10 (commits bdb6c25/d986289/b02d0fa). Since then creation/annotation/hatch/table/array/delete paths changed only by lint; move/copy/rotate/scale and all LISP-based edits (trim/extend/fillet/break/join/stretch), connection ProgID logic, DXF import and selection changed, so those are not covered by the live artifacts.

deduction.reason: Cap at 2 (reproduced, probe P09): LISP-driven trim/extend report success with no postcondition, even for nonexistent handles. Other edit paths are COM-only and were not executed.

items.scope_and_limits: No numeric tolerance/fit computation (draw_tolerance passes raw GD&T text). No evidence of displayed result after dimension-style or text-style edits. The demo image shows dimensions drawn outside the sheet frame that the verification did not flag. Live AutoCAD artifacts were recorded 2026-08-08..10 (commits bdb6c25/d986289/b02d0fa). Since then creation/annotation/hatch/table/array/delete paths changed only by lint; move/copy/rotate/scale and all LISP-based edits (trim/extend/fillet/break/join/stretch), connection ProgID logic, DXF import and selection changed, so those are not covered by the live artifacts.

deduction.reason: Withhold 3: no error/boundary behavioral evidence for annotation in AutoCAD, no tolerance/fit support and no post-edit display check.

items.name: Domain workflows
items.basis: The declared domain is mechanical drawings plus drawing understanding. Live artifacts show a three-view bearing housing and a flange-coupling assembly with BOM table and item leaders, and a VLM review grounded to handles with the section hatch correctly left ambiguous. Rule-based semantic detection (slots, bolt circles, walls, doors, title blocks) is tested on synthetic data. Strict pass: semantic/grounding suites ran green (454 passed, including PIL-based image-trace and VLM tests that CI skips). No new domain workflow evidence. Score unchanged.
items.scope_and_limits: Understanding evidence is on drawings the tool itself created, not foreign drawings. No P&ID, architectural room/opening or takeoff workflow with output evidence. Image-to-CAD tracing is tested on synthetic rasters only (PIL tests skipped in Linux CI).

deduction.reason: Withhold 3: no foreign-drawing or non-mechanical domain workflow with output evidence.

items.name: Transactions
items.basis: CADPlan validation, the allow_modify gate, failure-text/structured-failure detection and the rollback call are covered by monkeypatched tests that pass in CI. The live 90-step plan shows StartUndoMark/EndUndoMark succeeding. Strict pass: P06/P07 confirm the gates (unknown op, send_command, missing variable rejected; execute without allow_modify refused) and rollback on a failed step. Two defects were reproduced. P08: with rollback_on_high_severity_validation=True and post-plan validation passed=false with high-severity issues, execute returns ok=true and never calls rollback. P16: a real-dispatch CADPlan draw_line step with AutoCAD disconnected returns 'Executed 1 CAD plan steps' with save_as bound to 'layer:'.
items.scope_and_limits: Rollback is EndUndoMark plus one 'U' command; it reports success when the command is sent, without checking that the entities are gone. If StartUndoMark fails, execution continues with a warning. A live rollback smoke case exists in scripts/verify_cad_understanding_workflow.py, but no result is committed. Dry-run is static.

deduction.reason: Cap at 2: reproduced false-success. The advertised validation rollback is a no-op (P08), and a plan whose step drew nothing is reported executed (P16).

items.name: Intent and geometry
items.basis: Dimension binding compares dimension measurements and text overrides with bound geometry; mismatches become violated constraints, ambiguous bindings stay unknown, and unchecked postconditions are returned as ok=null ('requires rescan') rather than passed. The live demo checked 134 constraints (127 satisfied, 7 unknown, 0 violated). Strict pass: P03 binds an R6 override on an R5 circle as violated, a correct R5 as satisfied, and leaves a far-away dimension unbound/unknown. P04 flags zero-length/duplicate/overlapping lines while a clean drawing passes. P05 reproduces wrong identity capture: 'Inserted block DOOR at 100,200' yields handles ['100','200']. In P16 a real plan bound $l to 'layer:'.
items.scope_and_limits: Behavioral cases use synthetic SQLite fixtures with production code. Plan handle capture falls back to taking up to three hex-looking tokens from result strings, which can mis-bind save_as variables. Post-plan validation reads the SQLite cache, which holds input-argument geometry until a rescan. No tampering or saved-artifact check.

deduction.reason: Cap at 2: demonstrated fake-identity capture. parse_tool_result_handles turns coordinates or labels into handles that save_as variables then carry (P05, P16). Constraint and validation logic passed its probes.

items.name: Delivery
items.basis: DWG save, DXF export and an A3 PDF plot were delivered in the live demo; the DXF and PDF are committed, and the README reports an independent one-page landscape A3 check of the PDF. Export waits for the output file to appear. Strict pass: delivery (save/export) is COM-only and was not executed; no readback/hash path exists to probe. Score unchanged.
items.scope_and_limits: No delivery gate, source version or hash, readback of the saved file, DXF semantic parity or per-format check scope. save_drawing reports success when SaveAs raises no exception. A DWG export uses doc.SaveAs, which also re-points the active document. The verification report records no product SHA.

deduction.reason: Withhold 3: no readback, hash or parity checks on delivered files.

items.name: Foreign and abnormal inputs
items.basis: DXF passed to open_drawing is refused before AutoCAD is touched; import checks permission and file existence before creating a document, does not modify a non-empty template, and preserves the document and settings on failure (mocked). Scans report truncated=true past max_entities. Unitless legacy arc angles and unsampled splines are left unresolved instead of guessed (real code, synthetic data). Strict pass: P13 confirms .dxf is refused by open_drawing before AutoCAD is touched, and import_dxf is refused without allow_modify and for a missing file. P14 confirms an arc without an angle unit is not closed into a profile. The disconnected-backend case (P15/P16) is not handled safely. Corrupt or foreign DXF content cannot be exercised because import is COM-only.
items.scope_and_limits: No corrupted-file, unknown-entity, unit-mismatch or external-edit case is evidenced against AutoCAD. The README tells agents to rescan after external changes; the server does not detect them.

deduction.reason: Withhold 3: refusals are executed and correct, but abnormal backend state yields false success elsewhere, and no corrupt/foreign file content can be processed headlessly.

items.name: Backend contract
items.basis: cad-mcp-doctor and check_runtime_environment report missing or blocked dependencies (MCP v1 rejected, optional visual extras, strict startup preflight), with tests. The Windows release run executed doctor --json from a clean wheel. The live preflight artifact passed with AutoCAD. ProgID fallback and stale-proxy refresh have tests. Tool profiles are discoverable through recommend_cad_tools and get_tool_help. Strict pass: the stdio server started in the container with the repo's own COM stubs, negotiated protocol 2026-07-28 and exposed 116/213/324 tools for lean/core/full; headless tools answered correctly over stdio. With AutoCAD unavailable, postconditions are inconsistent: draw_line returns 'OK' with an empty handle (also over stdio), draw_circle raises, and other tools return failure text.
items.scope_and_limits: Postconditions are not consistent across tools (string vs dict results, trim/extend success without read-back). There is a single AutoCAD COM backend; no capability map per operation.

deduction.reason: Withhold 3: the missing-backend contract is inconsistent and includes a false 'OK' (stdio-output.json, P15). Discovery and preflight are credited.

items.name: Behavioral regressions
items.basis: 418 tests passed in CI on the pinned SHA. They include strong adversarial suites for topology, grounding and VLM safety, MCP v2 protocol and concurrency-serialization tests, LISP-literal injection tests and plan gating tests. Strict pass: executed `pytest -q -m "not autocad_com"` offline in Docker. 454 passed, 2 skipped (Windows-path test; pywin32 stdio launch), 0 failed, 480 subtests. With git absent, 25 agent-benchmark tests error, so git is an undeclared test dependency. The suite does not detect the disconnected-backend false OK (P15/P16).
items.scope_and_limits: The AutoCAD tool layer is tested through MagicMock controllers; test_all_interfaces is largely signature/consistency checks. 22 tests skipped in Linux CI (PIL and real stdio). No integration test runs against AutoCAD in CI, and no live smoke result is committed.

deduction.reason: Withhold 2: no real-backend integration tests; reproduced false-success paths are untested.

Strict pass: installed with `pip install -e ".[dev,visual]"` from unpinned ranges (mcp resolved to 2.3.0). The test suite additionally needs a git checkout and the git binary (25 errors without it).
items.scope_and_limits: No lock file or hashes. Live artifacts do not record the product commit or environment beyond the platform string. The agent-benchmark ledger is pending, with no results.

deduction.reason: Withhold 3: unlocked dependencies and no product SHA in recorded evidence.

items.basis: Per-push/PR CI completed successfully on the pinned SHA. The release workflow gates PyPI/registry publication on tests. items.name: Defaults and security
items.basis: SQL queries run under a SQLite read-only authorizer. Handles and numbers are validated before AutoLISP is built (tests). Tools carry readOnly/destructive annotations. Transport is local stdio only. Strict pass: P10 shows the LISP literal guards reject injected handles/numbers before anything is sent. P12 shows execute_query refuses INSERT/DELETE/ATTACH/writable PRAGMA/CTE-delete, and no file is created. P11 reproduces send_command forwarding an arbitrary AutoLISP (startapp "cmd.exe" ...) string unfiltered. The stdio check confirms send_command is registered in lean, core and full.
items.scope_and_limits: The code default profile is 'full', and send_command (raw AutoCAD command line, including AutoLISP) is exposed in every profile, even lean, with no denylist. open/save/export/import accept arbitrary absolute paths with no workspace scoping, and save overwrites silently with FILEDIA=0. Safety relies on client approval of annotations.

deduction.reason: Withhold 4 (reproduced): raw command/AutoLISP passthrough exists in every profile and paths are unscoped; the SQL and LISP-literal guards are credited.

items.name: Long tasks
items.basis: Tool calls are serialized on the event-loop thread (tested for concurrent calls). AutoCAD idle waits, save retries, and SQL timeouts and result caps exist. A rotating log records tool-call context. Scans are bounded with truncation reporting. Strict pass: the suite's concurrency-serialization and native-v2 facade tests passed. No cancellation/recovery path exists to probe. Unchanged.
items.scope_and_limits: No cancellation, lock or crash-recovery behavior. Rollback is best-effort and unverified. run_lisp treats any return to idle as success. No long-task output evidence beyond the live demo's multi-phase run.

deduction.reason: Withhold 3: no cancellation or recovery behavior, and timeouts are not evidenced on failure paths.

declared_contract: A local, handle-first stdio MCP server (Python, MCP SDK 2.x) that drives a running, licensed AutoCAD on Windows through COM, exposing 116/213/324 tools in lean/core/full profiles. It claims 2D drafting, editing, annotation, tables, blocks, layouts, plotting and export, plus 3D solids. It also claims a SQLite-backed drawing-understanding layer (CAD-IR, semantic graph, constraints, dimension binding, validation) and guarded CADPlans (validate, static dry-run, transactional execution through AutoCAD undo marks with best-effort rollback). Further claims are visual grounding and VLM-finding reconciliation, image-to-CAD tracing, and mechanical drawing workflows. The only backend is AutoCAD COM. It is explicitly beta, for operator-reviewed local workflows, with no formal standards compliance claimed.

serious_defects.description: With AutoCAD disconnected (no document), draw_line reports 'OK: drawn line' with an empty handle because drawing_tools uses the controller's {success: false} dict as if it were the entity. Reproduced in-process and over MCP stdio.

execute_cad_plan discards rollback_on_high_severity_validation; a plan whose post-validation has high-severity issues returns ok=true with no rollback. A plan whose draw_line step drew nothing (AutoCAD disconnected) is reported as executed.
parse_tool_result_handles turns coordinates or labels into handles ('100','200'; 'layer:'), so save_as variables can carry fake identities.
trim/extend (run_lisp edits) report success once the command queue is idle, without verifying target existence or geometry change.
serious_defects.reproduction: reproduced at wrapper level with a stub document (P09); real AutoCAD behaviour not executable here

serious_defects.description: send_command forwards any AutoCAD command/AutoLISP string unfiltered and is registered in every profile; file paths are not scoped.
serious_defects.reproduction: reproduced (P11 and the stdio tool listing)

limitations: No repository code was executed; scores rest on source reading, completed CI runs and committed artifacts.
All live AutoCAD evidence is historical (August 2026). Edit, connection, DXF import and selection code changed afterwards, and no live run at the pinned SHA is committed.
Unit tests for the AutoCAD tool layer mock the COM controller, so they evidence wrapper behavior, not CAD output.
Visual judgement of the demo PNG is a single reviewer's inspection.
The rubric's anchors were applied literally; the 324-tool count, star counts and README claims earned no points.
Strict pass: COM-backed behaviour was exercised only through stub documents or a disconnected controller, which shows what the wrappers report, not what AutoCAD does.
